title: Oil and gas concession rounds 5 to 13 (ANP)
what: Exploration and production rights over offshore and onshore blocks of Union-owned subsoil were sold by concession in rounds 5 to 13. Signing bonuses ran from R$ 27 million (round 5) to R$ 2.48 billion (round 11).
who_got: Petrobras, foreign majors and, from round 9 on, many small Brazilian firms. Winners are named only for round 7 (for example Petrobras, Petrogal, Devon, ENI, Shell, Koch, Repsol YPF, Statoil). Financing is not documented in the sources.
terms: The signing bonus was the only up-front price. No source values the blocks. ANP reports only the bonus, the minimum exploration programme and local-content offers.
mechanism: Concession model of Lei 9.478/1997. From round 5 the bonus, exploration programme and local-content offer were scored together. Minimum local content in round 5: 30% deep water, 50% and 60% shallow water, 70% onshore. Round 12 weights: 40% bonus, 40% exploration programme, 20% local content.
who_paid: The Union gave up subsoil rights in exchange for bonuses. Round 8 was stopped by a federal-court injunction after 38 blocks were sold. No rounds were held in 2009–2012.
after: After the 2007 pre-salt discoveries the government stopped concession rounds in the pre-salt area and moved to production sharing (see cessão onerosa and Libra). Local-content waivers per round and winner lists for most rounds were not found.
counter_view: ANP's stated aim of scoring exploration programme and local content in the bid was to raise exploration and local supply (ANP yearbook 2004). Low early bonuses may reflect frontier risk before the pre-salt was known (this is an interpretation, unverified).

title: BNDES export-service loans to Brazilian contractors abroad (Odebrecht, Mariel, Angola)
what: BNDES disbursed US$ 10.5 billion to finance engineering services exported by Brazilian contractors. Five contractors took 98% of it and Odebrecht took 76%.
who_got: Odebrecht 76%, Andrade Gutierrez 14%, Queiroz Galvão 4%, Camargo Corrêa 2%, OAS 2%. Foreign states such as Cuba (Mariel port) and Angola were the borrowers. Odebrecht was also the third-largest recipient of all BNDES disbursements in 2003–2018 (R$ 51.3 billion, domestic and export).
terms: Loans to foreign states, to be repaid. For Mariel, MDIC confirmed some Treasury transfers without return. Sources disagree on the size of the Angola exposure.
mechanism: BNDES export financing, with repayment risk on foreign states. A Treasury-backed export guarantee fund is mentioned in the notes (unverified).
who_paid: BNDES and the Treasury carry the default risk. From 2018 Venezuela, Mozambique and Cuba stopped paying (arrears US$ 554 million by June 2019).
after: Secrecy fight over BNDES files, CGU and TCU probes, and Odebrecht plea deals in Lava Jato.
counter_view: Aos Fatos: these were loans to be repaid, not donations. BNDES had received US$ 10.3 billion of the US$ 10.5 billion disbursed, so the loss was small. Only the Mariel Proex transfers were confirmed as non-repayable (Aos Fatos, https://www.aosfatos.org/noticias/e-falso-que-pt-doou-r-14-bilhoes-do-bndes-para-governo-de-angola/).

title: Petrobras contractor cartel and kickbacks (Lava Jato) and the leniency deals
what: Contractors inflated Petrobras contracts and paid 1-3% kickbacks to parties, according to plea testimony. Petrobras recognised a R$ 6.19 billion corruption loss in 2014. Later leniency deals with the main contractors agreed about R$ 8 billion, of which about R$ 1 billion was paid by mid-2022.
who_got: Odebrecht and Andrade Gutierrez led the cartel, per the Federal Police and prosecutors. Ex-director Paulo Roberto Costa said PP, PT and PMDB split Petrobras directorships to collect 1-3% on big contracts. Youssef said 60% of the bribe fed political agents.
terms: Costa said the 3% was embedded in contractor margins and denied overpricing at some works. The Federal Police estimated losses of up to 20% of contract values, while plea-bargainers admitted 3%. TCU found about R$ 4.2 billion of overpricing at three works alone (Rnest, Repar, Angra 3).
mechanism: Cartel in Petrobras tenders plus political division of directorships. Afterwards the Anticorruption Law (Lei 12.846/2013) allowed leniency agreements: first MPF agreements, then CGU/AGU agreements that credit the earlier ones, with Selic indexation. Firms may keep selling to the public sector.
who_paid: Petrobras (minority shareholders and the Treasury), Eletrobras and taxpayers. The notes also say workers lost jobs afterwards (not sourced).
after: Plea deals and leniency agreements followed. In 2022 the firms were trying to rewrite the agreements for longer terms or lower amounts.
counter_view: Costa said the 3% was embedded in contractor margins and denied overpricing at some works (Gazeta do Povo). Firms argue the sums cannot be paid while they are barred from contracts and that restructuring preserves jobs (Congresso em Foco, 13 Jun 2022).

title: PPP law and the first PPP, São Paulo Metro Line 4
government: Lula 1 (federal law); São Paulo state (Line 4 contract)
what: Lei 11.079/2004 created public-private partnerships with state payment guarantees. Line 4 of the São Paulo Metro (ViaQuatro) was the first metro PPP: private operation for 30 years.
who_got: The ViaQuatro consortium, which buys trains and systems and operates the line.
terms: No audited cost figure was found. A union publication says the government pays 80% of civil works, the rest is financed by BNDES over 30 years with the state as guarantor, and the state pays the shortfall if demand is lower.
mechanism: Sponsored and administrative concessions under Lei 11.079 of 30 Dec 2004. The state guarantees the payments. The public side builds tunnels and stations.
who_paid: The São Paulo state treasury carries demand and guarantee risk, according to the union text.
after: ViaQuatro later sought about R$ 500 million from the state for works delays (search result only), which shows risk also hit the private side. Total investment is given in the press as about US$ 2 billion (not verified).
counter_view: Pro-PPP view: private operation brought driverless trains and quicker works. The critical text is a union advocacy publication (metroviarios.org.br).

title: Public forest concessions (Lei de Gestão de Florestas Públicas)
what: Timber-management rights in national forests were granted for up to 40 years while the land stays public. Flona Jamari (RO) had 96,000 ha under concession in three management units.
who_got: Private timber firms. The 2008 Jamari tender covered three areas and five firms were qualified for the final stage. The notes' 'three firms' is corrected to three areas.
terms: Payment per area and volume. The notes' claim of about R$ 7 million a year from one forest is unsupported (the cited page was unrelated). JB 2013 says R$ 5.5 million had been paid in total up to 2012.
mechanism: Lei 11.284/2006, with tenders run by the forest service. Contracts allow up to 40 years.
who_paid: Outcome and community impacts were not researched.
after: By Nov 2021 there were seven forests with about 1.265 million ha and 21 contracts (Brasil61). A Saracá-Taquera (PA) south lot signed in Aug 2010 could not be confirmed.
counter_view: The law is defended as a way to fight illegal logging while keeping the land public (Brasil61). It is a weak 'handover' case.

title: Madeira River dams: Santo Antonio and Jirau (Rondônia)
what: Two large hydropower concessions on the Madeira River, with BNDES loans of R$ 6.1 billion (Santo Antonio) and R$ 7.2 billion (Jirau). Total investment was estimated at about R$ 28 billion.
who_got: Santo Antonio: Furnas 39%, a Banif/Santander fund 20%, Odebrecht Investimentos 17.6%, Andrade Gutierrez 12.4%, Cemig 10%, CNO 1% (public share 49% with Cemig). Jirau: GDF Suez, Camargo Corrêa, Eletrosul, Chesf, with Funcef and Petros in Camargo's stake.
terms: Santo Antonio won the 10 Dec 2007 auction at R$ 78.87/MWh (Exame: 78.90), 35% below an ANEEL ceiling of R$ 122 and 16.1% below the runner-up. No independent valuation was found.
mechanism: ANEEL auctions in 2007–2008 and BNDES project-finance loans.
who_paid: Displaced riverside residents and workers. The Union through Furnas' stake and BNDES financing (BNDES amounts for this point not opened). Workers rioted in March 2011 over conditions; BNDES kept disbursing.
after: MPF, public defenders and OAB-RO sued on 6 Mar 2014 after a flood. A court ordered help for about 10,500 displaced people and new impact studies within 90 days, under a R$ 100,000/day fine. The final outcome was not found. In July 2025 MPF sued Jirau for flooding beyond its licensed quota into Mapinguari National Park. Plea testimony alleges about R$ 80 million in bribes tied to Santo Antonio; the accused dispute it.
counter_view: The low auction tariff gave consumers cheaper energy. Later cost overruns suggest the bid may have been unrealistic (unverified). The bribery claims are allegations, not findings.

title: Treasury funding of BNDES and PSI subsidised credit ('bolsa-empresário')
what: The Treasury borrowed at market rates and lent to BNDES at the lower TJLP rate. Treasury injections into BNDES were R$ 441-455 billion in 2008–2014. Estimates of the subsidy cost differ by orders of magnitude.
who_got: Mostly large firms (67.9% of disbursements in 2012 went to large firms, per Márcio Garcia), including the firms in the JBS, Oi, EBX and Votorantim cases. Named beneficiaries of PSI were not extracted.
terms: Cost depends on method: R$ 11.6-15.9 billion in 2008–2010 (Mansueto Almeida), R$ 44.5 billion versus R$ 180.7 billion over four decades (Coutinho), R$ 205.6 billion in 2008–2022 (IBRE). PSI 2011 cost was R$ 11.8 billion (SPE) or R$ 19.2 billion (Treasury method).

title: Terra Legal: land regularisation in the Amazon (MP 458/2009, Lei 11.952/2009)
what: Federal public land in the Amazon was titled to occupants, up to 15 fiscal modules and a maximum of 1,500 ha. TCU data cited by MPF show 28,331 titles covering 2,057,119.95 ha by 31 Dec 2017.
who_got: Occupants of federal public land who were there before 1 Dec 2004 (article 5 IV).
terms: Free up to one fiscal module. Above that, paid titles priced from the minimum value in the Incra reference table, adjusted for time, region and size. Resale is restricted for 10 years, and over 4 modules can be transferred after 3 years.
mechanism: MP 458/2009 converted into Lei 11.952/2009. Later the cut-off date moved to 22 July 2008 (Lei 13.465/2017, from a search summary), and the 2,500 ha ceiling was added by a congressional amendment in that conversion bill, not in MP 759.

title: Caixa buys a stake in Banco Panamericano
what: In Dec 2009 Caixa (via Caixapar) bought 35.54% of Banco Panamericano for R$ 739.272 million. Fraud was found in Sep-Nov 2010. Caixa held 49% of voting capital.
who_got: Grupo Silvio Santos received the price.
terms: The Central Bank estimated a hole of R$ 2.5 billion. New management put the shortfall at R$ 4.3 billion. Prosecutors alleged balance-sheet fraud of at least R$ 3.8 billion in 2007–2010, and a court convicted seven former directors. title: Belo Monte dam (Xingu, Pará)
what: The concession went to Norte Energia, led by Chesf/Eletrobras, at the April 2010 auction. BNDES approved R$ 22.5 billion in Nov 2012 over 30 years, the biggest loan in its history.
who_got: Norte Energia. The shares quoted in the notes (Eletronorte 19.98%, Eletrobras 15%, Chesf 15%, Petros 10%, Funcef 10%) are from June 2017, not 2010. Others held Belo Monte Participações (Neoenergia) 10%, Amazônia Energia (Cemig/Light) 9.77%, Aliança Norte (Vale/Cemig) 9%. Norte Energia was majority state-owned.
terms: Winning bid R$ 77.97/MWh versus a ceiling of R$ 83 (6.02% discount); the subtitle of the source says 78.03. Cost estimates rose from R$ 19 billion at the auction to about R$ 26-30 billion. Economist Rogério Werneck argued a cost-reflective tariff was at least R$ 100/MWh (not verified).
mechanism: A legislative decree (DL 788/2005) authorised works without prior Indigenous consultation, followed by an ANEEL auction and BNDES credit. The MPF suit filed in 2006 lost 2-1 at TRF-1 on 9 Nov 2011; judge Selene Almeida voted to annul the decree until Indigenous people were heard. ILO Convention 169 was ratified in 2003. The final merits outcome was not confirmed.
who_paid: Indigenous and riverine people (the Xingu basin has 24 ethnic groups in 30 Indigenous Lands), the Treasury through BNDES and state shareholders, and the environment.
after: Plea deals: Camargo Corrêa executives said 1% of the contract went to PT and PMDB politicians. Andrade Gutierrez's deal cites about R$ 150 million in bribes. A claim of R$ 15 million to Delfim Netto is denied. TCU opened an audit in June 2015 (result not found). The MPF said BNDES showed no evidence of viability and risk analysis (reported via WRM, not opened). Contractors asked for another R$ 1 billion (unverified).
counter_view: The government and developers say there is no direct impact on Indigenous lands, but MPF disagrees (Outras Palavras guide). The plea-deal bribe claims are allegations from testimony. MDB denied them, Delfim Netto's lawyers say he did consulting work and paid taxes, and he told police he got R$ 240,000 from Odebrecht. The opposing bidder, Belo Monte Energia (Andrade Gutierrez, Furnas, Eletrosul), lost.

title: Airport concessions: Guarulhos, Viracopos, Brasília (2012), Galeão and Confins (2013)
what: Concessions of 20 to 30 years. The 6 Feb 2012 auction offered R$ 24.535 billion in total. The 22 Nov 2013 auction of Galeão and Confins offered R$ 20.839 billion in total.
who_got: Guarulhos: Invepar/ACSA. Brasília: Inframerica. Viracopos: Aeroportos Brasil (Triunfo, UTC, Egis). Galeão: Odebrecht Transport with Changi. Confins: CCR 75%, Flughafen Zurich 24%, Munich 1%. Infraero kept 49% of each concessionaire (ITL; Galeão confirmed). Financing for Galeão and Confins was not established.
terms: Premiums over the minimum were large: Guarulhos 373% (R$ 16.213 billion on a minimum of R$ 3.424 billion), Brasília 673% (R$ 4.5 billion on R$ 582 million), Viracopos 159% (R$ 3.821 billion), Galeão 293.9% (R$ 19.018 billion), Confins 66% (R$ 1.82 billion). The true Galeão and Confins minimums are uncertain: Exame's numbers and the premium maths do not agree.
mechanism: Federal concession run by ANAC, with a fixed grant (outorga) plus a variable contribution. The Lei 13.448/2017 relicitation framework was later used for Galeão.
who_paid: Users and the public side bore the aftermath: forgone grant payments and Infraero's 49% exposure; BNDES was the main creditor of Viracopos. Odebrecht exited Galeão in 2017.
after: Viracopos: shareholders asked to return the concession in 2017 (year unconfirmed), the concessionaire filed for judicial recovery on 7 May 2018 (debt about R$ 2.88 billion, mostly BNDES) and the plan was approved on 14 Feb 2020, leading to Brazil's first airport relicitation. Galeão: Changi (51% after buying out Odebrecht in 2017) asked ANAC on 10 Feb 2022 to return it, claiming a R$ 7.5 billion imbalance; ANAC had denied the rebalancing. A 30 Mar 2026 auction reportedly gave Galeão to Aena for R$ 2.9 billion (not confirmed by the fact-check). Confins was not returned and got a R$ 60.7 million recomposition in Nov 2022.
counter_view: The government framed the premiums as proof of competition and low taxpayer cost (bids about five times the minimum, EBC). The concessionaires blame the 2014–16 recession and Covid. ANAC held the demand shortfall was the concessionaire's risk. Critics read the big premiums as over-bidding (the winner's curse).

title: MP 579/2012 (Lei 12.783/2013): electricity concession renewals
what: Generation and transmission concessions were renewed early for up to 30 years at lower revenue, with indemnity for unamortised assets and lower sector charges. The promised bill cut was more than 16%.
who_got: Consumers and electro-intensive firms got lower tariffs. Concessionaires such as Cesp, Cemig and Copel resisted. This is a reverse case.
terms: MME expected indemnities of about R$ 20 billion and Eletrobras expected about R$ 30 billion. Eletrobras later got about R$ 14 billion, then about R$ 20.8 billion after MP 591 (search summary).
mechanism: MP 579/2012, converted into Lei 12.783/2013, with MP 591/2012 correcting transmission indemnities (investments up to 31 May 2000, paid over 30 years, IPCA).
who_paid: The Treasury (through CDE transfers) and Eletrobras. No consolidated Treasury figure was found. Eletrobras's 2012 loss was R$ 6.88 billion and its shares fell about 28% around the announcement (search summary only).
after: Critics say the cut was artificial and was followed by a 'tarifaço' in later years.
counter_view: The opposing view is that the state forced renewal at below-market indemnities (Poder360 and Acende Brasil, via search summary, not opened).

title: Forest Code 2012 (Lei 12.651): amnesty for past deforestation
what: The new Forest Code reduced the penalties and restoration duties for clearing before 2008. Soares-Filho and colleagues (Science, 2014) estimate it amnesties 29 million ha illegally cleared before 2008.
who_got: Rural landowners, large and small, whose legal-reserve debts for pre-2008 clearing were reduced.
terms: Restoration needed falls from 50 to 21 million ha (-58%), and 88 million ha remain legally clearable. Protection from penalties applies to infractions before 22 June 2008 if the owner joins the regularisation programme (PRA).
mechanism: Lei 12.651/2012. On 28 Feb 2018 the STF upheld most of it: of 23 provisions, 18 were constitutional and 5 unconstitutional.
who_paid: The environment, the climate and downstream water users.
after: The STF held that it is not a true amnesty, because owners keep penalties if they fail the regularisation terms.
counter_view: Tereza Cristina (Frente Parlamentar da Agropecuária) called the amnesty partial, with legal certainty for farmers and over 90% of producers in the rural registry (CAR). Agroicone's Rodrigo Lima said pre-2008 penalties are forgiven only if owners follow the 2012 rules. The Science authors say only 1% of cropland sits in areas needing restoration. Environmentalists such as ISA's Nurit Bensusan say it invites future deforestation (Câmara; Brasil Agro).

title: Federal highway concessions, third round
what: 30-year toll concessions with duplication obligations in the first five years. Example: Concebra (BR-060/153/262, 1,176.5 km, Triunfo), won in 2014.
who_got: Concessionaires such as Triunfo (Concebra). Financing via BNDES and a 15% internal return were not confirmed.
terms: Low-toll-bid model. The notes' signing date of 31 Jan 2014, the five-year duplication duty and the BR-163 details come from a page that is now 404, so they are unconfirmed.
mechanism: Federal toll concessions awarded by ANTT (Edital 004/2013 for Concebra).
who_paid: Users paid tolls without the promised works. BNDES exposure was not quantified.
after: Six concessions of 2013–14 struggled to meet the main duplication requirement. ANTT approved relicitation of BR-060/153/262 in 2021, split into Rota do Zebu (BR-262 MG, auctioned 2024) and Rota Sertaneja (BR-153/262 GO-MG). The remaining 211.6 km of BR-060/153 stays with Concebra in a TCU consensual-solution process (2026).
counter_view: Not found. The usual argument for low-toll-bid auctions was not sourced. A primary source such as an ANTT or TCU audit of the third round is still needed.
